title: What is a religion?
examples: What do religions have in common?
What is the biggest religion in the world?
What is the difference between monotheism and polytheism?

explain.say: A religion is a shared way of answering life's biggest questions, like why we are here, what matters most, and how we should live. Most people in the world belong to one.

draw.text: Shared answers to life's big questions

explain.say: Most religions are built from the same few blocks: beliefs, worship, a community, rules for living well, sacred stories and books, and festivals.

draw.text: Same blocks, different shapes in every faith

explain.say: Religions see the divine in different ways. Some teach that there is one God, some honour many gods or forms of the divine, and some, like Buddhism and Jainism, do not centre on a creator god.

items: One God: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Sikhism
Many forms of the divine: many Hindu traditions

draw.text: Monotheism means one God; polytheism means many gods.

explain.say: Religion also shapes daily life: how people pray, what they eat, which days they rest, and how they mark birth, marriage and death.

items: Holy days | Shabbat, Sunday, Friday prayers

explain.say: In 2020, about three in four people in the world belonged to a religion. Christians and Muslims were the largest groups, followed by Hindus and Buddhists.

draw.label: Share of the world in 2020, in percent (Pew Research)

explain.say: Religions differ a lot, yet many teach a version of the golden rule: treat others as you would like to be treated. Learning about them helps us understand our neighbours with respect.

draw.text: We study religions to understand, not to rank them

faq.q: What do religions have in common?
faq.a: Most religions share beliefs about life's big questions, ways of worshipping, a community of followers, rules for living well, and sacred stories or books. Many also teach kindness to others, like the golden rule.
asks: What are the features of a religion?

faq.q: What is the biggest religion in the world?
faq.a: Christianity is the largest, with about 2.3 billion followers, close to 29 percent of the world in 2020. Islam is second with about 2 billion, then Hinduism with about 1.2 billion.
asks: Which religion has the most followers?
What is the most popular religion?

faq.q: How many religions are there in the world?
faq.a: There are thousands of religious traditions, large and small. But most religious people belong to a handful of big ones, like Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism and Judaism.
asks: Number of religions in the world?

faq.q: What is the difference between religion and faith?
faq.a: Faith usually means a person's trust or belief, often in God or the sacred. Religion is wider: it includes that belief plus shared practices, worship, community, teachings and traditions.
asks: Is faith the same as religion?

faq.q: What is the difference between monotheism and polytheism?
faq.a: Monotheism is belief in one God, as in Judaism, Christianity, Islam and Sikhism. Polytheism is belief in many gods. Many Hindus honour many deities, and often see them as forms of one ultimate reality.
asks: One god or many gods meaning

faq.a: Hinduism is often described as the oldest living major religion, with roots going back more than 3,000 years. Judaism and Zoroastrianism are also very ancient.

faq.q: What does it mean to be an atheist or agnostic?
faq.a: An atheist does not believe in God or gods. An agnostic thinks we cannot know for sure whether God exists. In 2020 about 24 percent of people said they had no religion, though some of them still hold spiritual beliefs.
asks: What about people with no religion?

faq.q: Why do people follow a religion?
faq.a: People give many reasons: it offers meaning and hope, a sense of the sacred, guidance on how to live, a close community, and traditions shared with their family across generations.
asks: Why do people believe in God?

faq.a: A sacred text is a book or collection of writings a religion holds holy, like the Bible for Christians, the Quran for Muslims, the Torah for Jews, the Vedas and Bhagavad Gita for Hindus, and the Guru Granth Sahib for Sikhs.
Worship means showing love, honour and devotion to God or the sacred. It can be prayer, singing, reading scripture, making offerings, meditation, or gathering together at a place of worship.

faq.q: What are places of worship called?
faq.a: Christians gather in churches, Muslims in mosques, Jews in synagogues, Hindus in mandirs or temples, Sikhs in gurdwaras, and Buddhists in temples and monasteries.

faq.q: Is Buddhism a religion or a philosophy?
faq.a: Many people call Buddhism a religion, because it has teachings, monks and nuns, temples, festivals and practices. Others describe it as a philosophy or way of life, since it does not centre on a creator god. Both views are common.

The golden rule is the idea that you should treat others as you would like to be treated. A version of it appears in many religions and philosophies, from Christianity and Judaism to Confucianism, Islam and Hinduism.
asks: Treat others as you want to be treated

faq.q: Why should we learn about religions?
faq.a: Religions shape art, history, laws, festivals and how billions of people live. Learning about them, with respect and without ranking them, helps us understand our neighbours and the wider world.

facts: In 2020, Christians made up about 28.8 percent of the world, Muslims 25.6, the religiously unaffiliated 24.2, Hindus 14.9 and Buddhists 4.1 percent (Pew Research).
Jews were about 0.2 percent of the world in 2020, about 14.8 million people (Pew Research).
Monotheism means belief in one God; polytheism means belief in many gods.
Buddhism and Jainism do not centre on a creator god.
A version of the golden rule appears in many religions and philosophies.

quiz.say: Which of these is a place of worship for Sikhs?
quiz.show: A Sikh place of worship is a…
quiz.why: Sikhs worship in a gurdwara, which means the door of the Guru.

wrong.0: A synagogue is the Jewish place of worship.
wrong.2: A mosque is the Muslim place of worship.
wrong.3: A mandir is a Hindu temple.

quiz.say: A religion teaches that there is only one God. Which word describes it?
quiz.show: Belief in one God is called…
quiz.why: Mono means one, so monotheism is belief in one God, as in Judaism, Christianity, Islam and Sikhism.

wrong.0: Polytheism is belief in many gods.
wrong.1: Atheism is not believing in God or gods.
wrong.3: Agnosticism is the view that we cannot know whether God exists.

quiz.say: Buddhism does not centre on a creator god. Many still call it a religion. Why?
quiz.show: Why is Buddhism usually called a religion?

options.show: Because it has a creator god after all
options.say: Because it has a creator god after all

options.show: Because it has teachings, practices, community and festivals
options.say: Because it has teachings, practices, a community and festivals

options.show: Because it is the largest religion
options.say: Because it is the largest religion

quiz.why: A religion is more than belief in a god: shared teachings, worship and meditation, monks, nuns and lay followers, and festivals all make Buddhism a religion for most scholars.

wrong.0: Buddhism does not centre on a creator god; that is the point of the question.
wrong.2: Christianity is the largest religion; Buddhists are about 4 percent of the world.
wrong.3: Buddhism began in South Asia, in what is now Nepal and India.
